explanation: The pole fires on the pivot word of a precautionary clause: the item that marks something as to be prevented, avoided or watched out for. It peaks on the negated purpose clause (the 'to' of 'not to VERB', with 'not' itself elevated, and the "'t" of don't/won't), on an avoidance/prevention/refusal predicate (avoid, prevent, stop, refuse, reject, deny, oppose, resist, ignore) standing in a modal, 'want to' or purpose-'to' frame, on recommendation frames ('it is best to', 'the key is to', 'you'll want'), and on the 'for'/'on'/'to' of a look-out phrase ('look for', 'watch out for', 'keep an eye on', 'attend to'); it stays near zero on the same words in episodic statements of completed events ('They prevented the fire', 'He avoided the question'), on bare modality with an ordinary verb ('He must go to the store', 'You should drink more water every day'), and on danger described without any precaution ('The storm destroyed every house on the street'). A weaker second mode (0.3-0.6 of max) fires on the newline that ends a colon-terminated label or heading in formatted text ('Safety Guidelines:\n'), much less on ordinary sentence-final newlines (0.2-0.3 of max).
